title: Visualisation Services
headline: To see the structure in things.
intro: Visualisation should reveal relationships, not merely decorate a report.
summary: From renderer-neutral user interfaces to 3D observation and scientific explanation, visualisation in Alchemy is an act of making evidence legible.

sections.heading: The interface is not the truth
sections.body: Wire UI separates semantic application state from its rendering. A browser, a native desktop renderer or another access point can display the same meaningful application elements without becoming their owner.

sections.heading: Spatial worlds and live observations
sections.body: Wire3D and related visualisation work explore geometry, movement and observation. Viewpoints are useful when they disclose provenance, timescale and coordinate semantics rather than pretending all data belongs to one flat picture.

sections.heading: Designed for people and agents
sections.body: An interface may be visual for a person or semantic for a machine. Both must preserve the same application authority, admissible actions and evidence of what was actually presented.
